hypotheses.title: R(+)-SCH-23390 hydrochloride extends lifespan in C. elegans
hypotheses.claim: Administration of R(+)-SCH-23390 hydrochloride extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. The compound acts as a geroprotective intervention in this organism.
hypotheses.rationale: Modulation of dopaminergic signaling can influence feeding, stress responses and metabolic rate, all of which regulate aging. Pharmacological adjustment of such pathways may therefore prolong survival.
hypotheses.prediction: Treated nematodes will show a statistically significant increase in median and maximum lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Synchronize worm populations, expose them to R(+)-SCH-23390 hydrochloride throughout adulthood, and perform standard lifespan assays with survival scoring every two days.

hypotheses.title: Mycophenolic acid extends lifespan in C. elegans
hypotheses.claim: Administration of mycophenolic acid extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. The compound acts as a geroprotective intervention in this organism.
hypotheses.rationale: Restriction of nucleotide availability can activate nutrient-sensing and stress-response pathways linked to longevity. Mild metabolic inhibition through such compounds may therefore slow the aging process.
hypotheses.prediction: Treated nematodes will show a statistically significant increase in median and maximum lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Synchronize worm populations, expose them to mycophenolic acid throughout adulthood, and perform standard lifespan assays with survival scoring every two days.

hypotheses.title: Mycophenolic acid extends lifespan via purine biosynthesis inhibition
hypotheses.claim: Administration of mycophenolic acid extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans by inhibiting de novo purine biosynthesis. The lifespan extension depends on this specific metabolic mechanism.
hypotheses.rationale: Slowing de novo purine synthesis imposes a controlled metabolic constraint that can engage conserved longevity pathways, including autophagy and stress resistance. Mechanistically targeted metabolic restriction may therefore extend survival.
hypotheses.prediction: Treated nematodes will show lifespan extension that is abolished when de novo purine biosynthesis is experimentally restored.
hypotheses.experiment: Compare lifespan of worms treated with mycophenolic acid alone versus mycophenolic acid supplemented with exogenous purines or hypoxanthine that bypass the inhibited pathway.

hypotheses.title: FCCP extends lifespan in C. elegans
hypotheses.claim: Administration of FCCP extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. The compound acts as a geroprotective intervention in this organism.
hypotheses.rationale: Mild uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation reduces mitochondrial membrane potential and reactive oxygen species production. Such controlled mitochondrial stress can activate adaptive responses that promote longevity.
hypotheses.prediction: Treated nematodes will show a statistically significant increase in median and maximum lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Synchronize worm populations, expose them to FCCP throughout adulthood, and perform standard lifespan assays with survival scoring every two days.

hypotheses.prediction: Treated nematodes will show a statistically significant increase in median and maximum lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Synchronize worm populations, expose them to sesamol throughout adulthood, and perform standard lifespan assays with survival scoring every two days.

hypotheses.title: FCCP extends lifespan in C. elegans at high doses
hypotheses.claim: Administration of FCCP extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans at high doses. The lifespan-extending effect is specific to the high-dose range of this intervention.
hypotheses.rationale: Sufficient uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation may be required to trigger mitohormetic adaptive responses that promote longevity. Higher doses could reach the threshold needed for such protective signaling.
hypotheses.prediction: Nematodes receiving high doses of FCCP will show a statistically significant increase in lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Perform lifespan assays across a dose range of FCCP, including high doses, and compare survival curves of each dose group against untreated controls.

hypotheses.title: Mycophenolic acid shortens lifespan in C. elegans
hypotheses.claim: Administration of mycophenolic acid shortens lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. The compound acts as a life-shortening intervention in this organism.
hypotheses.rationale: Excessive inhibition of de novo purine biosynthesis can deprive cells of nucleotides needed for DNA repair and cell maintenance. Such metabolic insufficiency may accelerate tissue decline and shorten survival.
hypotheses.prediction: Treated nematodes will show a statistically significant decrease in median and maximum lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Synchronize worm populations, expose them to mycophenolic acid throughout adulthood, and perform standard lifespan assays with survival scoring every two days.

hypotheses.rationale: Uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation impairs ATP production and energy-dependent cellular maintenance. Sustained energy deficit may accelerate physiological decline and shorten survival.
hypotheses.prediction: Treated nematodes will show a statistically significant decrease in median and maximum lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Synchronize worm populations, expose them to FCCP throughout adulthood, and perform standard lifespan assays with survival scoring every two days.
